proposals: The US Federal Trade Commission and Department of Justice should publish, for each completed transaction notified under the premerger-notification programme, the parties, closing date and a deal-value band, so that mergers of private-equity platforms like Brand and Safway, whose terms were never disclosed, leave a public price trail.

The US Securities and Exchange Commission should require listed buyers of material stakes in private companies to disclose the target’s revenue and headcount at the transaction date, so that a valuation such as BrandSafway’s $6.7 billion in 2019 can be set against the business it actually bought.

The SEC should require listed acquirers to state the price and EBITDA multiple of material acquisitions in their filings, making standard the disclosure United Rentals gave for NES Rentals — the only one of the three 2017 deals in this post where a reader could check price against earnings.
